newsitem.title: USA: Clinton - jobs growth reflects strong U.S. economy.
newsitem.headline: Clinton - jobs growth reflects strong U.S. economy.

text.p: President Clinton said on Friday that the December jobs report showing 262,000 new jobs being created reflects the overall strength of the U.S. economy.

During a meeting with top corporate executives to discuss ways to create jobs for ex-welfare recipients, Clinton also said that Federal Reserve Board Chairman Alan Greenspan and Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin noted in recent discussions with him that inflation pressures that would normally occur in such a good jobs market are currently lacking.

"I basically believe as long as we're competitive, as long as our markets are open, as long as we are reaching out to new markets around the world, as long as we are seeing American workers continue to upgrade their skills and American businesses employ technology and better production techniques and improve their productivity that we can keep this going without undue inflation," Clinton said. "At least now there is no evidence (of inflation)."

Clinton told reporters ahead of the corporate executives meeting that his fiscal 1998 proposed budget will include incentives "attractive to the private sector" to encourage the hiring of welfare recipients.
"Welfare reform, if it is going to work, will have to have the leadership of the private sector in turning welfare checks into pay checks," Clinton said.
He said he would discuss the welfare issue with the corporate leaders attending the meeting.
Clinton, when asked about the announced resignation of Federal Reserve Governor Lawrence Lindsey, said he would deal with that and another Fed vacancy "in a timely fashion."
